newsitem.title: UK: Euro-bourses cast off rate fear and rebound.
newsitem.headline: Euro-bourses cast off rate fear and rebound.

text.p: Fears the United States might raise interest rates to stem inflationary pressures made European financial markets wobble on Friday, but a measure of calm returned as Wall Street clawed back some of the damage inflicted on Thursday.
U.S. stocks shot higher with bonds in the first few minutes of trading after weaker than expected producer prices (PPI) data for February and capacity utilisation eased fears of a rate tightening.

The dollar, which dipped in Europe after the PPI data was released, later recovered, although it failed to reach peaks scaled after Thursday's U.S. retails sales figures that were seen as hardening the argument for the Federal Reserve to raise rates.
The PPI's biggest fall since October 1994 leaves the Fed in a difficult position as it prepares for its policy-setting meeting on March 25, New York economists and traders said.
Despite evidence of a strong economy, there are few signs of price pressures actually rising.

"It gets back to the core question as to whether or not they (the Fed) should be pre-emptive and they are probably doing some soul-searching right now," said Tom Benfer, a director of foreign exchange at Bank of Montreal in New York. "If they tighten the rate structure, politically they will get a lot of flak."
A rally in Philip Morris shares led the Dow's rebound which also boosted European stock markets that had already decided they should not get too rattled by Wall Street's 160 point slump on Thursday.
After an initial sharp markdown in European stock values, investors kept their nerve and the main markets slowly recouped most of their losses.

"People used the opportunity to bank some profits this morning, but we recovered because market makers want to keep fairly flat books and not get caught short of stock," said one senior trader in London.
Among Europe's big three bourses, Paris suffered the worst during the morning, but by 1500 GMT the blue chip CAC-40 index was back in the black by nine points at 2,641 points.
Shares in Assurances Generales de France fell 3.59 percent to 206.8 francs after the group expressed interest in bidding for privatisation target GAN.
The German market, which was the worst performer of the big three on Thursday, got a strong boost from the U.S. data and ended bourse floor trade with a gain of 9.48 points at 3,359.29.
Share prices rose strongly in later screen-based trade with the IBIS DAX index putting on 36 points.
"We are clearly in a period of extreme volatility. We are going to have to get used to it," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Chemical shares rebounded from lows hit this week after disappointing news from Hoechst AG that it had abandoned plans to list its HMR drugs unit.
Daimler-Benz AG got a major boost after a well-received meeting with analysts at Goldman Sachs on Thursday and news of plan to set up a traffic navigation joint venture with Deutsche Telekom.
Daimler was up 2.70 marks at 129.15 marks in the afternoon.
British shares recouped virtually all their losses and were hovering just below Thursday's closing levels by mid-afternoon, while government bonds had firmed with U.S. treasuries.
Traders said domestic factors had helped to support the London market.

"The UK is flush with cash," said Corey Miller, strategist at CL Laing. "There's a possibility of more special dividends...returning cash to institutions, and with interest rate expectations being reined back in the UK, people should still be looking to put that money back in the UK market."
The dollar ebbed and flowed through the day, but moved back to around 1.7050 marks and up to 124 yen in the afternoon.

"The retail sales report was yet another catalyst to point out to people that the same fundamental dollar-bull story is as valid now as it was a month ago," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7055 marks and 124.05 yen, compared with Thursday's late European levels of 1.7030 marks and 122.92 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 2.5 points, or 0.06 percent, at 4,395.2
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 9.66 points, or 0.37 percent, at 2,641.76.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trade up 9.48 points, at 3,359.29. In screen trade, the IBIS DAX was up 36.82 points at 3,404.64.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $352.80, down 20 cents from the morning. Silver was off two cents at $5.275.
